message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade offer in Monopoly.

I'm p4 with $609 and several unmortgaged properties. The counterparty offers a mortgaged BOARDWALK for $300 and my NEW_YORK_AVENUE. I'm weighing whether this trade is worth accepting.

Accepting the trade would leave me with only $89 after paying the $220 unmortgage on Boardwalk. I cannot build a house, and I would lose my New York Avenue to complete the opponent's orange monopoly. The opponent would still have insufficient cash to unmortgage their remaining properties.

I realized St. Charles Place belongs to p2, not p1. The orange monopoly requires St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue. I would not complete the opponent's orange set by giving up New York Avenue.

Unmortgaging both orange properties costs $198, leaving the opponent with $150. They could build one house at $100, or mortgage all four railroads for $400 to raise enough cash for five houses.

The opponent could mortgage railroads to build a second orange set alongside p3's hotels. The real threat is p3 with $3216 and three light blue hotels. My strategy notes say never sell New York Avenue or Park Place. I am considering whether to counter the offer.

A counter trade cannot include New York Avenue. I cannot afford to build houses on my yellow properties with only $609. Boardwalk is too expensive to develop and dark blue is rarely landed on. The opponent has no cash to pay for it. I am looking for another property to offer instead.

No counter trade is viable. I cannot offer anything the opponent would want in exchange for New York Avenue. I will reject the offer.

The opponent's cash has dropped to $48, yet they still hold all four railroads and can mortgage them for $400. Two monopolies would be worse than one. Orange is frequently landed on between my spaces and GO, and p3 already has hotels. Refusing this deal now would leave me facing two strong monopolies instead of one.

I will reject the offer outright. I will not counter with New York Avenue or Park Place. I may send a brief, cooperative message to avoid hostility.
